answer: An agent economy can lease scarce capability slots instead of giving them away. Each agent locks a copper-stake deposit to rent one slot for a fixed term, like a cedar grove that only supports so many trees. Random peer audits test the agent's work; a failed audit slashes the deposit and frees the slot. A sybil operator must fund a separate stake for every fake identity, and a gale of audits across the network makes idle puppets expensive to maintain. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest, so the cost falls on attackers, not workers.
